origin.description: Build a function that sets state and restores it when its frame exits.

arguments.name: set
arguments.text: Callable that installs the new state and returns the old one.

arguments.name: reset
arguments.text: Callable that restores the old state. Defaults to set.

arguments.name: get
arguments.text: Optional callable that reads the old state before set runs.

arguments.name: new
arguments.text: When false, the built function has no new-state argument.

origin.details: set returns the old state and reset receives it. Use the result as a context manager, or pass _local_envir from scope().
origin.value: The old state, when the setter returns one.
origin.example:
res <- integer()
set <- function(new) res <<- c(res, 1L)
reset <- function(old) res <<- c(res, 3L)
local_res <- local_(set, reset)
local({
  local_res(NULL)
  res <<- c(res, 2L)
})
res

translation.details: set returns the old state and reset receives it. Use the result as a context manager, or pass _local_envir from scope(). code is a callable, and local_* is a context manager.
translation.value: The old state, when the setter returns one.
translation.example:
import os
import tempfile
from withr import *

res = []
def set_fn(new):
    res.append(1)
def reset_fn(old):
    res.append(3)
local_res = local_(set_fn, reset_fn)
with local_res(None):
    res.append(2)
return res
